title: ldconfig-pulse-debug-notes
content:
Purpose: live scratchpad for weird OOMs that correlate with system ldconfig/cache pulses and intermittent libcuda/libcudart mismatches. Goal is to capture commands tried, flaky outputs, hypotheses, and an ordered next-steps checklist.

Summary of symptom (short):
- Worker processes serving small-batch generation occasionally fail with out-of-memory errors inside CUDA allocation path even when NVML reports free memory. Failures often coincide with rolling restart of worker fleet or nightly ldconfig runs on some hosts.
- Error manifests as: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.12 GiB (GPU 0; 47.68 GiB total capacity; 35.4 GiB already allocated)" but nvml shows only ~18 GiB used.
- Strace of process at failure shows intermittent open() of /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 -> broken symlink or older soname in cache depending on timing.

Useful command probes (what I ran):
- nvidia-smi (quick snapshot):
  $ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.used,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv
  index, name, memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB], driver_version
  0, A100-SXM4-80GB, 18432 MiB, 81000 MiB, 535.86

- nvml allocation check via small python snippet (works most times):
  import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); h=pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0); print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(h))
  -> shows ~60 GiB free on host while process still OOMs.

- ldd on the running binary and on torch extension (to check which libcuda is resolved):
  $ ldd /opt/conda/envs/py/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep cuda
  libcudart.so.11 => /usr/local/cuda-11.7/lib64/libcudart.so.11 (0x00007f...)
  libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f...)
  
  BUT sometimes after an ldconfig run the same ldd shows libcudart.so.11 => /opt/cuda-legacy/lib/libcudart.so.10 (mismatch!).

- checked ldconfig.cache snapshots around time window: /etc/ld.so.cache (binary) -> used strings/grep to map libcudart entries. Observed that when some maintenance job writes a new /etc/ld.so.conf.d/overlay.conf pointing to /opt/cuda-legacy, the cache switches and containers without restart pick up different library paths.

Repro attempts (deterministic-ish):
1) Start container with host driver 535.x and /usr/local/cuda-11.8 present, but /opt/cuda-legacy also mounted by k8s daemonset (admin test).
2) Warm model (LLM) on GPU; memory stable ~18 GiB used.
3) Run sudo ldconfig (as part of node maintenance) that updates cache to prefer /opt/cuda-legacy first.
4) Worker attempts a new allocation and fails with CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN inside cudaMemcpyAsync, backtrace points to libcudart mismatched symbols.

Observed logs / error snippets captured: (excerpts)
- /var/log/syslog:
  Mar  6 03:02:11 host-12 maintenance: wrote /etc/ld.so.conf.d/overlay.conf
  Mar  6 03:02:12 host-12 ldconfig[2341]: cache updated

- container stderr at failure time:
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/opt/service/runner.py", line 421, in process_batch
      out = model.generate(batch)
    RuntimeError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
  -------------
  CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
  libcudart.so.10: cannot allocate memory in static TLS block

- dmesg (rarely shows anything): no kernel OOM messages, no IOMMU issues.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Mixed CUDA user libraries (libcudart, libcuda) between host and container cause ABI/symbol mismatch; when ldconfig overlay switches, containers that rely on host cache (via bind mounts) can pick up wrong sonames at runtime without restart, leading to undefined behavior that looks like OOM.
2) The ldconfig pulse is temporarily replacing symlinks to older cuda installs (legacy toolchains), which are missing TLS or symbol versions needed by newer CUDA runtime -> allocations fail due to internal runtime state mismatch, not real memory shortage.
3) Some process (node agent) is writing /etc/ld.so.conf.d fragments with incorrect ordering during upgrades; ordering-dependent cache leads to nondeterministic outcomes across nodes.
4) In a few cases, the Python interpreter and a preloaded C extension hold references to old symbols that get re-resolved to incompatible .so during the cache update leading to partial relocation failures.

Commands and small experiments to validate hypotheses (what next):
- Reproduce in safe env: create minimal container that binds /usr/lib and /usr/local/cuda* from host and run ldconfig inside host to flip cache. Observe via strace whether open() switches target.
- Run: LD_DEBUG=libs python -c 'import torch; torch.cuda.current_device()' before and after ldconfig to see which SONAMEs resolve.
- Toggle LD_PRELOAD to force host libcuda version inside container (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1) and see if problem disappears -> suggests resolution path ordering issue.
- Add startup check in runner that asserts: soname(libcudart) path matches expected and refuses to serve if mismatch. Simple: readlink for libcudart.so.* in /proc/self/map_files? or ldd output parsing.
- Try running with --gdb and attach to process on allocation failure to inspect symbol tables and TLS allocations (painful but definitive).

Temporary mitigations tested so far (results):
- Restarting container after ldconfig fixes the process (consistent). Means newly spawned processes pick up current cache mapping and are fine. Not acceptable for zero-downtime.
- Pinning LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container to /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64 prevents the issue (no ldconfig-dependent switch). But hard to enforce across all images and hides underlying root cause.
- Daemonset that ensures /etc/ld.so.conf.d/ overlay fragments are ordered and canonical reduced frequency but didn't eliminate.

Notes on oddities:
- Sometimes ldd on the binary reports the older path but strace open() shows the new path (contradiction) - suspect ld.so.cache binary vs runtime lazy binding interplay.
- When I intentionally remove /opt/cuda-legacy from host, error disappears 100%. Strong evidence that coexistence + cache updates matter.

Possible long-term fixes:
- Avoid exposing host /usr/local/cuda* dirs into containers (mount namespaces) unless absolutely required by k8s drivers. 
- Add an init-time soname check in our runner and in Dockerfile set consistent rpath or LD_LIBRARY_PATH to pinned cuda install.
- Educate SRE to avoid ad-hoc ldconfig updates during maintenance windows or to coordinate with workloads.
- Build a small LD cache watchdog that signals pods to restart gracefully when cache changes (last resort).

Immediate TODO (ordered):
1) Create minimal repro container image and test flip sequence (Asha) - target by 2026-03-08.
2) Draft a short note for SRE playbook to avoid ldconfig writes during busy windows and to not mount legacy cuda dirs (Priya).
3) Implement simple soname-check in runner (< 2hrs) that logs mismatch and refuses new allocations (Liam).
4) Open GH issue for packaging consistent runtime that sets rpath (Asha).

Slack notes / comms to send once repro exists: short post in #eng-serving-runtime with steps to reproduce and a link to the minimal image, tag SRE.

Final stray thought: could also be interaction with systemd-tmpfiles or a cron job that rotates symlinks in /opt. I want to add a cronmon job to capture /etc/ld.so.conf.d changes (mtime) and /sbin/ldconfig invocations across nodes to correlate.

-- end of scratchpad --
